clinicalPearls: A progressive disorder of the His-Purkinje conduction system causing widening QRS, bundle branch and fascicular block, and increasing degrees of atrioventricular block over time
Loss-of-function variants in SCN5A (the cardiac sodium channel gene) are the classic inherited cause, with several other genes implicated
Presents with syncope, presyncope or bradycardia-related symptoms, and may cause sudden death if complete heart block occurs without escape rhythm
The structurally normal (idiopathic) form is termed Lenegre disease; a variant with fibrocalcific involvement of the conduction system is Lev disease
SCN5A conduction disease overlaps with Brugada syndrome and other sodium-channel phenotypes, sometimes in the same family (overlap syndromes)
Serial ECGs are key because the conduction disturbance worsens with age
Management is guided by symptoms and the level and severity of block, with cardiac pacing central to symptomatic or high-grade conduction disease
reference.pathophysiology: Progressive cardiac conduction defect reflects impaired impulse propagation through the specialised conduction tissue. In the SCN5A-related form, loss-of-function variants reduce cardiac sodium current, slowing conduction velocity through the His-Purkinje system and predisposing to bundle branch and atrioventricular block. Ageing-related fibrosis of the conduction system compounds the genetic defect, so block worsens over time, giving the characteristic progressive course. Because the same sodium-channel dysfunction underlies Brugada syndrome, families may show mixed conduction disease and Brugada-type phenotypes. When advanced block develops without an adequate ventricular escape rhythm, profound bradycardia and asystole can cause syncope or sudden death.
additionalDifferentials: Ischaemic conduction disease from coronary artery disease
Iatrogenic block from atrioventricular nodal-blocking drugs
additionalInvestigations: Serial 12-lead ECGs to document progression of conduction block
Ambulatory ECG monitoring to capture intermittent high-grade block
Echocardiography to exclude structural or infiltrative heart disease
Cardiac MRI where infiltrative or inflammatory disease is suspected
Genetic testing (SCN5A and related genes) with cascade family screening
Electrophysiological study in selected cases to localise the level of block
redFlags: Syncope with high-grade or complete atrioventricular block
Very wide QRS with alternating bundle branch block
Family history of pacemaker requirement or sudden death at a young age
Coexisting features suggesting an infiltrative or lamin-related cardiomyopathy
reference.prognosis: With timely recognition and pacing for symptomatic or high-grade block, prognosis is generally favourable, but untreated advanced conduction disease carries a risk of syncope and sudden death, and overlap phenotypes may add arrhythmic risk.
pitfalls: Assuming conduction block is purely degenerative and missing an inherited SCN5A basis
Overlooking an overlapping Brugada or lamin phenotype that changes risk stratification
Failing to monitor serially so progressive block is detected late
Not screening relatives despite a clear autosomal dominant pattern
references: ESC guidelines on cardiac pacing and conduction disease
management: Permanent pacemaker implantation is the mainstay for symptomatic or high-grade atrioventricular and His-Purkinje conduction block
No drug corrects the conduction defect; avoid agents that further impair conduction such as sodium-channel blockers and atrioventricular-nodal blocking drugs where possible
Consider a defibrillator rather than a pacemaker alone where a coexisting Brugada-type phenotype or other arrhythmic and sudden-death risk is present
Serial 12-lead ECGs and ambulatory monitoring to track progression and capture intermittent high-grade block
Assess for and manage associated arrhythmias and overlapping sodium-channel phenotypes
SCN5A and related gene testing with cascade family screening and genetic counselling
Advise on syncope safety and escalate urgently for pacing when block advances
